What Illustrate can bring forward

Diagram Design has seven standalone types and three variants that Illustrate lacks. The highest-value fixes recover source content during import and preserve appearance during export.

Which fixes carry over

Each reproduced gap below compares the existing Illustrate worktree with upstream at the pinned commit. The regression table separates tested behavior from code and documentation findings.

Reproduced

Import loses source details

The current Mermaid extractor loses or rejects valid source content. draw.io and Excalidraw each have import cases that alter the result.

  • Mermaid loses body text in repeat state descriptions, Unicode ER names, ER aliases and cardinality, and sequence branch labels and autonumber metadata. BOMs, edge IDs, apostrophes, invisible links, spaced labels and hyphenated IDs also reproduced gaps.
  • draw.io loses relative child position and table-row shape, resurrects hidden cells, strips literal angle brackets and emits a traceback for an unwritable destination. Its existing arrow direction, absolute nesting and digest escaping passed.
  • Excalidraw loses outer group reporting and text bound to unsupported containers. It reads wrapped visual lines in place of authored originalText. Its bidirectional cycles and nesting-limit diagnostic passed.
  • Port reader changes per format and keep current JSON keys, Markdown digest conventions and redraw routing. Add the paired fixtures before changing code.

#349 #410 #413 #418 #421 #422 #444 #445 #446 #447 #455 #458 #466 #468 #469 #472 #479 #494 #496 #504 #505 #510 #512

Reproduced

SVG appearance and accessibility

The SVG exporter carries some page CSS but does not namespace defs. Two exported figures can share marker IDs. Named and numeric HTML references can produce invalid or different SVG text.

  • The probes also found defs inserted before the first title, selection of a commented figure, an accepted invalid viewport and lost comment-like text inside quoted CSS selectors.
  • Nested SVG icons, double-hyphen comments, tested CDATA style handling, original root-ID CSS, print scope, RGBA alpha and quoted comma/space selectors passed the sampled cases.
  • Port SVG extraction, naming and serialization in small hunks inside export_diagram.py. Keep the existing CLI, data-motion attributes, arrow marker roles, registry and animation entry points. Test two inline figures together and end-to-end GIF output.

#235 #314 #321 #348 #411 #414 #417 #423 #426 #432 #486

Mixed evidence

PNG sizing and static capture

A legal filename with # and % passed on Windows. Exact viewBox pixel sizing and fractional scale 1.25 failed against the upstream behavior.

  • The current PNG path uses default page loading and networkidle. Upstream has a bounded font wait and explicitly requests the complete static motion frame. These two behaviors are source findings in this review.
  • Port bounded wait and deterministic static rendering first. Review fractional PNG scale separately as an additive CLI choice. Preserve integer scales and existing GIF timing and scale behavior.

#183 #322 #348 #354 #398 #411

Reproduced and inspected

Authoring and verifier gaps

Illustrate’s checks miss several visible problems that upstream already catches.

  • Paired samples reproduced duplicate SVG naming IDs, right-edge clipping, overflowing label text, truncated HTML, misread single-quoted geometry, and false paint findings inside defs.
  • The OAuth verifier accepts a solid access-token return and a guard present only inside an HTML comment. Port visible element and return semantics into the current sequence gate.
  • Chart and projection follow-ups include exact decimal conservation, collapsed scale, hidden ancestor labels, opacity composition, CSS quoted-value handling and geometry attributes. Replay the landed tests against the existing theme-aware verifiers before writing changes.
  • Reuse local svg_scan and theme_tokens. Keep Arabic and custom-font layouts, hand and motion scope, and technical-color checks in the acceptance corpus.

#327 #350 #351 #405 #408 #409 #433 #440 #467 #470 #484 #507 #513 #514 #524

Available upstream

More source formats

PlantUML redraws sequence and class diagrams through a dedicated extractor. Mermaid quadrantChart targets the existing Quadrant diagram.

  • Ship PlantUML with its command routing, text and Markdown digest and clear unsupported-kind diagnostic. Cover .puml, .plantuml, .pu and fenced sources.
  • Add Mermaid Quadrant after the shared parser fixes. Retain the existing Mermaid, draw.io and Excalidraw entry points. Pass the resolved theme and existing output dials to the new routes.

#358 #522

Targeted follow-ups

Documentation and packaging

Correct the zero-based Loop station explanation, the DP Integration focal arrowhead and the wiretext dependency wording. The current exporter already enforces exclusive output flags and the local label-mask rule already names resolved paper.

  • Borrow the render-and-look step and type checklist. Keep the current three galleries, package metadata, versioning, CI and SkillEvaluator work. A lightweight count check should track standalone entries as the catalog grows.
  • Upstream named client profiles, brand palette changes, gallery redesign, host manifests and Doctor tooling are optional compatibility or product decisions. Sanduq already owns its theme policy, galleries and host install paths.

Adoption plan

Proposed sequence for your review. Apply the fixes and additions in sanduq-skills, then update the pinned vendored copy in sanduq from a released bundle.

Baseline

Record the approved scope

Capture current package and gallery behavior before the first patch.

  • Record hand, motion, GIF and technical-color checks.
  • Keep upstream patch IDs and MIT attribution.
  • Run the source and vendored test suites in a fresh checkout.
Reliability

Land the fixes first

Make import, export and render validation reliable before widening the catalog.

  • Split import by format, then SVG/PNG and verifier changes.
  • Port landed behavior from consolidation PRs.
  • Keep controller and exporter contracts covered.
First diagram batch

Ship the broad-use types

Start with Steps, Service blueprint, Unit Grid and Architecture containment.

  • Port existing light, dark and full examples.
  • Add hand coverage and theme-aware verification.
  • Wire the original and both alternate galleries.
Second diagram batch

Add the deeper grammars

Bring Requirement traceability, Event modeling, Schedule network, Box plot and Arc diagram after the first batch.

  • Confirm SBGN demand and PlantUML timing.
  • Add Mermaid Quadrant after parser fixes.
  • Release Illustrate, update vendor.lock.json via vendor.py, then verify the Spec Kit commands.

Keep the existing capabilities

  • Both editorial and technical-color families, including toolbar Copy, PNG and PDF.
  • All light, dark, full and handwritten paths. The current editorial gallery includes 64 -hand.html files.
  • Controlled HTML motion and reduced-motion behavior. There are 10 -animated.html examples.
  • Animated SVG and GIF CLI flags, arrow styles, timing, frame rate, light/dark GIF output and registry sidecars.
  • Tracked project YAML, the Cobalt, Emerald and Sanduq presets, custom themes and remote/local/system font policies.

Release checks

  • Baseline selection, rendering and export across both families and all existing presentations.
  • Each new grammar gets a reference, light/dark/full examples, handwritten coverage, a budget, gallery registration and a type-specific verifier.
  • Run local regression cases and upstream-derived fixtures through installed paths. Verify reduced motion, complete static PNG, standalone SVG and actual GIF frames.
  • Open all three galleries and render representative outputs in Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Exercise Cobalt, Emerald and a dark/system-font theme.
  • After bundle release, sync the pinned extension, run vendor verification in a fresh checkout, and exercise Spec Kit generate, import and export commands.
Files and integration points
WorkIllustrate integration
ImportPort interpreter behavior into scripts/mermaid_extract.py, drawio_extract.py and excalidraw_extract.py with focused comparison fixtures. Add a PlantUML extractor and reference only for the approved scope.
SVG, PNG and validationKeep scripts/export_diagram.py as the public entry point. Preserve animate_export.py and sidecars. Land small extraction, serialization and static-capture changes plus tests. Extend self_check.py, verify-geometry.py and related gates through their existing CLI paths.
CatalogRegister new types in SKILL.md, references/type-index.md, the layout budgets and variants reference. Update assets/index.html, index-variation-1.html and index-variation-2.html, then cover assets with type, geometry, theme and render checks.
DownstreamAfter approval and a source release, use python extensions/scripts/vendor.py sync --source <skills-checkout> --input illustrate --ref <release-tag> in sanduq. Validate the lock and run the extension tests. Keep the current package and command names.

Theme migration check

Temporary Steps example passed through the current theme tool.

The test caught a palette gap. Cobalt applied the paper and type, but the upstream accent #bf4520 and its tint survived. Cobalt resolves to #2563eb. Convert colors and fonts to Sanduq roles during the port and verify the rendered result in each theme. Upstream palette change #369

Windows vendoring baseline. The current vendor.py check reports 58 mismatched SVG icon files. All 58 match the lock after CRLF → LF normalization and their committed Git blobs already match the lock. Use a fresh checkout when validating the release so line-ending drift is visible separately from the port.

What was compared

The three source snapshots and how the review distinguishes a confirmed gap from a candidate patch.

  • Diagram Design d74d8c2d, version 2.6.168, with 776 tracked paths and 473 commits in main ancestry. Reviewed the packaged skill, verifiers, import/export tooling, manifests, gallery routes, changelog, CI and PR history. Pinned upstream source
  • sanduq-skills at 7f6b6fae including working-tree edits already underway when the comparison began. sanduq at 00100086 pins Illustrate to illustration-tools-v3.7.1 at 150f808b. Both checkouts were read as-is for this review. Illustrate source repository
  • Catalog comparison uses upstream’s 51 type references and Illustrate’s advertised 44 types. Illustrate stores eight chart variants in separate references and has a type index, so a raw filename count would overcount its standalone types. The upstream skill’s opening prose still says “Fifty”; its type table and schedule-network change identify 51. Upstream type guide #527
  • The previous standalone Architecture diagram, Process flow diagram and Diagram Design paths are already consolidated in Illustrate. This review preserves their editorial and technical-color routes. Sanduq skill documentation
  • Each merged PR uses the merge commit’s first-parent diff. Each unmerged PR uses its head compared with main ancestry. File matching normalized CRLF. The full ledger shows current counterparts and the original changed paths. The paired probes are representative coverage. 86 rows with related paths are marked for comparison during implementation, and the remaining rows record confirmed coverage, gaps, feature decisions, upstream-only work or closed proposals.
  • Illustrate baseline tests passed 231 of 231 in sanduq-skills and 18 of 18 in sanduq. All ten upstream type and variant verifiers passed on their shipped examples. The current animated GIF exporter produced a 1000 × 600 GIF with 20 frames.
  • Existing third-party notices cover the upstream MIT license from Cathryn Lavery. Carry the license and applicable asset credits with any adopted material and cite source commits in each port. The embedded gallery screenshots are from the upstream MIT repository or were captured from its shipped examples. Upstream MIT license
